One of the two statements has to be corrected, and the code (`bindingSecret` in github-auth.guard.ts) matches the later one, so line 110 is the stale/incorrect claim in the canonical subsystem doc for this control.

samples.summary: Wrong home for app-wide cookie policy: `secureCookies`, `loginCookieName`, `loginCookieOptions`, `loginCookieValues`, `joinLoginCookieValues`, `bindingSecret`, `stateSignature`, `consentToken`, `secretEquals` and the cookie-name constants all live in a GitHub-specific *guard* file, and `auth.controller.ts` now imports `secureCookies` from it to decide the `Secure` flag of the ordinary **session/refresh** cookies. A guard should not be the module of record for the deployment's cookie-security predicate; this change already establishes the pattern of a small dedicated module (`src/logging/log-safe-url.ts`), so an `auth/login-cookies.ts` would fit the layering better.
samples.evidence: auth.controller.ts imports 13 symbols from './github-auth.guard', including `secureCookies` used by `baseCookieOptions()` for `wafflebase_session`/`wafflebase_refresh`.

samples.summary: Scope/coupling: `SECRET_PATH_SEGMENTS` hardcodes controller route shapes (`share-links/:token/resolve`, `invites/:token/accept`) inside a logging utility, so the logging module now silently depends on the router's URL vocabulary with nothing that fails when a new credential-in-path route is added or an existing one is renamed. The round-2 acceptance item only asked for granting *query parameters* outside `/auth` (`?token=`); the path-segment table is beyond it and introduces the sync burden without any enforcement (no lint/test ties it to the controllers).

Scope creep relative to both originating todos: neither `20260812-cli-login-loopback-binding-todo.md` nor `20260811-cli-error-envelope-command-todo.md` asks to change the `Secure` semantics of the existing session/refresh cookies, yet `baseCookieOptions()` switches them from `NODE_ENV === 'production'` to the new `secureCookies(GITHUB_CALLBACK_URL scheme)` predicate. This changes behavior for every existing deployment (e.g. an https deployment that configures an internal `http://` callback URL now loses `Secure` on its session cookie). It is documented in backend.md, but it is an unrequested behavioral change to an unrelated control riding on a login-binding branch.

The new frontend contract — the login page reading `?error=login_state` and rendering an alert — is recorded only on the backend side (`docs/design/backend.md`), not in the canonical frontend design doc that owns the `/login` route and states the frontend "handles the full auth lifecycle". The consumer half of a cross-package contract has no home in docs/design/frontend.md.
samples.evidence: docs/design/frontend.md:45 `PUB --> LOGIN["/login → Login"]`; grep for `error=`/`login_state` across docs/design matches only backend.md:168

samples.summary: Acceptance criterion "`wafflebase login` against a backend that ignores both parameters fails closed with a message naming the cause" is met only after the timeout, and the timeout was raised from 30s to 5 minutes in the same change — so a user on an old backend now waits five minutes before seeing the diagnostic, even though the unbound callback (`state === null`) is observed immediately. Failing fast on the first unbound code, or shortening the wait once one is seen, would satisfy the criterion's intent rather than its letter.
samples.evidence: `sawUnboundCode` is only consulted in the CALLBACK_TIMEOUT_MS handler (CALLBACK_TIMEOUT_MS = 5 * 60 * 1000)

samples.summary: Layer fit: a full hand-written HTML+CSS user-facing page (the CLI consent interstitial) is now rendered from the REST backend, which otherwise serves JSON only, while the frontend package owns all user-facing auth UI and the design system. The origin constraint (the confirm cookie is a backend-origin cookie) makes this defensible, but it duplicates a bespoke stylesheet that also exists in the CLI's own success/spent-link pages and bypasses the design system entirely; worth an explicit note or a frontend-hosted alternative.
